title: Strict scalar-extension square for the specified quotient-cone augmentation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $W=X,Y$ put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $B_{F,W,m}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $F=E,L$ and $m\geq1$, with quotient projections $\pi^F_{W,m}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}$ on completed-coefficient module complexes, transporting the action along the ring isomorphism $c_F:g^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}\simeq\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,X}$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. These maps satisfy $\pi^F_{X,m}c_F=c^g_{\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m}g^{-1}(\pi^F_{Y,m})$. Tensor products below are sheaf tensor products and their total complexes [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Let $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ and $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X$, with the chain isomorphism $b_P:Z\to G_LQ$, $g^{-1}p\otimes c_L(g^{-1}s_0)\mapsto g^{-1}(p\otimes s_0)$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model]. For $F=E,L$ and $M=P,Q$, respectively, put
$$D_m^F(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}}B_{F,Y,m}),\qquad A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_mD_m^F(M)\to\prod_mD_m^F(M))[-1],$$
where $g_{F,m}^*$ is finite-coefficient module pullback, $\operatorname{Res}^F_m$ restricts along $\pi^F_{X,m}$ and $s$ is induced by the actual quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Denote by $a^E_P:G_EP\to A_E(P)$ and $a^L_Q:G_LQ\to A_L(Q)$ the specified chain augmentations of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b): their shifted-product coordinate is zero and their $m$-th unshifted coordinate is $g^{-1}x\mapsto(g^{-1}(x\otimes1))\otimes1$.

Let $d_m:D_m^E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to D_m^L(Q)$ and $\delta_P:A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to A_L(Q)$ be exactly the same-index tower and whole-cone maps of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha]. Thus on local tensors
$$d_m(((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s)=(g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_{X,m}(s)),$$
and $\delta_P$ applies $\prod_md_m$ to both cone coordinates, using the finite-free tensor/product identifications. Then there is an equality of actual chain maps of $S_X$-complexes
$$\delta_P\circ(a^E_P\otimes_{R_X}S_X)=a^L_Q\circ b_P:Z\longrightarrow A_L(Q).$$
Both sides have shifted-product coordinate zero; their common $m$-th unshifted coordinate on $y\otimes s$, for $y=g^{-1}p$ and $s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0)$, is
$$(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes\pi^L_{X,m}(s)\ \in g_{L,m}^*(Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}).$$
Here $Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$ uses $R_Y\to B_{L,Y,m}=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_{Y,m}$, and $p\otimes1$ in the displayed formula is in this latter complex. The equality concerns the entire cone with its fixed zero shifted coordinate, before localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For ordinary completed scalar extension, pure tensors generate after sheafification. Prove s tensor x = s times (1 tensor x) by linearity of sheafification and the canonical object transport. Naturality of the sheafification unit and canonical object transport shows that 1 tensor x commutes with restriction to any site object. Thus equality of completed-linear maps can be checked on the unit tensors.

proof.text: For each level n, compare completed tensor(theta_E,n) followed by the normalized tower map with b followed by theta_L,n. On 1 tensor x, the defining theta formula is restriction of the finite pullback generator at the canonical comma arrow. Naturality moves the tower map through this restriction. CompletedFormula for b at scalar 1 and ScalarPullbackGeneratorFormula at a=b=s=1 give identical finite generators, since all coefficient ring maps preserve 1. Linearity and tensor generation from Step 1 give equality of these chain maps.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product); agent calculation of the normalized comparison.

proof.text: The augmentation has nth first projection theta_n and zero second projection by mappingCocone.lift. The normalized cone isomorphism has the canonical tensor/product map in both coordinates; the strict tower map induces the diagonal product map on the Roos cone. Composing its first coordinate with the nth product projection therefore tensors the old nth projection and then applies the nth tower map. Its second coordinate is the tensor of the old second coordinate followed by the two product maps. These formulas follow by associativity, the stated cone-coordinate equations, and Pi.lift_π and Pi.map_π.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit); elementary coordinate computation in the fixed mapping cocone.

proof.text: Compare the two composites degreewise. After each first product projection, Step 3 reduces the left composite to completed tensor(theta_E,n) followed by the nth tower map, and reduces the right composite to b followed by theta_L,n. They agree by Step 2. Both second coordinates vanish by Step 3, additivity of ordinary tensor, and zero_comp. Termwise product extensionality and mappingCocone.id_X determine each degree map from these two coordinates. HomologicalComplex.Hom.ext gives the strict chain-map equality.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit); elementary product and mapping-cocone extensionality before localization.

proof.text: For the displayed common section formula, first project the right composite: the augmentation projection is theta_L,n. Write its input as c_L(s0) times the unit tensor using Step 1. Completed-linearity of b and theta moves this scalar outside the composite. CompletedFormula at s0=1 identifies b of the unit tensor with the unit tensor over Y, giving exactly the displayed expression. The completed scalar action on the restricted finite pullback is already through its quotient projection, so no additional balancing or coefficient-square theorem is necessary.

Step 2: the shifted coordinate of a^E_P is 0 by def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison(b), and δ_P applies ∏d_m to both coordinates, so it stays 0 and matches the 0 of a^L_Q. Step 3: putting ā=b=1 into the d_m formula of the alpha node gives (g^{-1}(p⊗1))⊗π^L_{X,m}(s). Step 4: b_P(y⊗s)=g^{-1}(p⊗s_0). Under the alpha identification (p⊗s_0)⊗1 becomes p⊗π^L_{Y,m}(s_0), and moving that factor across the finite pullback tensor gives c^g g^{-1}π^L_{Y,m}(s_0)=π^L_{X,m}c_L(g^{-1}s_0)=π^L_{X,m}(s), which is the stated structure equation. This uses ρ_m=π^L restricted to R_Y, valid since ϖ_E^mO_E⊂ϖ_L^mO_L. Step 5: extensionality into products and cone summands, degree by degree.
